Frustration boiled over after the match when fans stormed the pitch. One supporter approached Onana from behind, phone in hand, appearing to film or take a photo. Tech Report: Kansas City Current's grit earns them spot in NWSL Championship while Gotham's logistics problems linger

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2257 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, NEW YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches.
  • "I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune mentioned post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".
  • Industry observers note that icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, NEW YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune mentioned post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

Industry observers note that icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game proposal that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during Fresh York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

It has been revealed that "We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins noted. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

The introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness issues over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

"I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill stated. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

It has been revealed that in other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

Industry observers note that gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two important blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of New York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

Sources indicate that in the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

"As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas said. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match blueprint that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

It has been revealed that the Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

"Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a initiative," Armas said. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

Recent findings suggest that gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while presently headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

According to recent reports, "Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros said. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

More importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up strategy for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull Fresh York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

"I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce said. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

Industry observers note that the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

According to recent reports, "I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros said. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

According to recent reports, "Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that this Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that it could keep them at the top end of the table for a good while longer. They have already shown they can defeat Arsenal in a one-off match and they look to have the ingredients to stay the pace with them. In Fabian Hürzeler they have one of the brightest young coaches in the Premier League and he has a squad that are all on the same page.

Industry observers note that leicester upset the odds 10 years ago with a settled team, while this Brighton team has a deeper squad. When the substitutes came on in the second half, they slotted into a well-rehearsed system.

In a recent development, “We faced adversity. There was a little bit of luck but in the end they deserved it because they worked hard for it,” stated Hürzeler. “I want players who want to compete, to dominate. They all have the winning mentality inside of them. These kinds of performances are not about one or two players, everyone has to stick together.”.

Recent findings suggest that hürzeler has played down a title challenge but his team have been among the most impressive in the first part of the season. The German coach, 33, has been in English football for two years but has learnt rapidly the tried-and-tested response of taking each game as it comes. Next is Getafe in the Europa Conference League on Thursday.

According to recent reports, while Hürzeler was reluctant to name individual performers, Dutch goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen was another key player in this win. He kept out Iliman Ndiaye and repelled Erling Haaland, who lost a physical battle with Lewis Dunk. “You’re going down with the Palace,” chanted the jubilant Brighton fans, with City now losing two Premier League games in a row.

City head coach Enzo Maresca will be content with the number of chances his team created but there must be concerns at the other end. He tried a change of formula, dropping Marc Guéhi to the bench for the first time this season, yet his team were still prone to individual errors.

“We are the second team in scoring in the Premier League. We are scoring goals but in this moment we are conceding silly goals. We can avoid that,” Maresca mentioned. His team have conceded 10 goals in their last six games, which is not the foundation of a title challenge, even if City have been stacking up points.

It has been revealed that maresca picked a midfield that cost £327m to recruit this summer, with Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi picked together for the first time. There were some signs they could all play together, although City looked more dangerous when Rayan Cherki came off the bench to break up the trio.

Pascal Gross cost a nominal fee when he returned to Brighton but his hard work and intelligent passing means Brighton can control periods of the game even against the very best.

According to recent reports, the goal came when Brighton switched play from a free-kick, although City thought Anderson was victim rather than perpetrator. Former Inter Miami winger Gómez provided the cross that opened up City, with Gianluigi Donnarumma guilty of not coming out to claim the ball, then Matheus Nunes slipped at the vital moment.

Recent findings suggest that “Unfortunately it is happening for our players but I think it is part of the game, part of football, it happens many times against us, we need to analyse and understand what we can do better,” Maresca added. City also felt Dunk used his arm to block the ball in the penalty area, although no spot-kick was given.

Recent findings suggest that it was a sweet goal by Ayari, who had missed a penalty in the shoot-out last week when the teams played in the EFL Cup. Brighton stayed in Manchester after the defeat, masterminding a win that means they have now defeated all of the traditional heavyweight teams in the Premier League.

Industry observers note that “I wasn’t aware of that. For me it’s more crucial, not about history, it’s about giving something back to the supporters. They’ve spent a lot of time and money,” Hürzeler said.

“We’ll take it game by game. See what happens because we have loads of games. Just focussing every day on what’s ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season. We are happy with the way we are playing - not just the results but the way we are playing too. We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things.”.

In City-related matters, Jack Grealish is battling for his future next season and faces becoming the Premier League’s most high-profile free agent following his breach of discipline at Everton.

The 31-year-old, who became the first £100m signing by an English club in 2021, is out of contract in eight months and his hopes of staying on Merseyside took a hit when the club decided he would not play in the Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.

While City head coach Enzo Maresca described Grealish as “a good boy with a big heart”, there are no signs of him getting a contract extension at the Etihad Stadium after being loaned out in the last two seasons.

Grealish is expected to be fined by Everton for an unauthorised absence from training and it is unclear when he will be back in David Moyes’ squad, with the club facing Newcastle again on Monday in the Premier League.

He had started the previous four matches and a return to playing regularly will be the key to securing a club next season.

“It is not correct to talk about Jack as he is an Everton player and I don’t have all the information,” said Maresca, who worked with Grealish when he was in Pep Guardiola’s backroom staff. “I still think he is a good guy, a good boy with a massive heart.”.

Industry News: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.
  • In a recent development, "Faith does not justify exclusion.
  • Sources indicate that "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related issues and the athletic performance of individual players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

In a recent development, "Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice. Nmecha's first documented "Crowns down celebration" was at the 2026 World Cup, for which "The King's Return" campaign was released.

Sources indicate that "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related issues and the athletic performance of individual players. We remain committed to this approach," the statement continued.

"However, when it comes to our club's values, discrimination, and the question of what view of humanity is fostered within and around Borussia Dortmund, we cannot and will not remain silent.".

The fan club states their concern is not with Nmecha being a devout Christian, but rather his public support for "The King's Return" campaign, which the supporters club noted "gives us cause to reassess the situation.".

This campaign, according to research by German public broadcaster ARD in the summer of 2026, was designed by the "Ballers in God" (BIG) network. BIG was founded in 2015 by footballer John Bostock, a devout Christian who wanted to create a community where professional footballers could strengthen each other in their faith, pray together, and read the Bible. In over a decade since, the BIG community has grown to nearly 800,000 followers on Instagram.

Nmecha issued a response on social media not long afterwards, writing:.

"I've been told that my most recent goal celebration has led to some misunderstandings," Nmecha wrote.

"My message was never intended to spread intolerance, discrimination, or hatred in any form. As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for every person—regardless of where someone comes from, what they believe in, or what worldview they hold.".

Reports suggest that both the board at Dortmund and Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp will speak to Nmecha on the matter in the coming days.

The fan club say their criticism is "directed at religious networks that, under the guise of faith, promote a worldview in which people are devalued or marginalized because of their sexual orientation, gender identity, lifestyle, or personal choices... When religious beliefs are used to deny people their dignity or equality, that is where our tolerance for intolerance ends.".

It has been revealed that here, they are referring to the recent ARD investigation. That work revealed the homepage for "The King's Return" campaign featured a link to a live counseling chat run by US-based evangelical nonprofit Groundwire. During the investigations, counselors told reporters that abortion is "Satan's plan" and that homosexuality is a sin.

Industry observers note that borussia Dortmund's statement of core values commits the club to diversity, human rights, and inclusion regardless of gender, sexual orientation, faith, or background. The club's largest and most influential fan group also promotes progressive, anti-fascist, and inclusive values. It is also part of a wider fan landscape in Germany where club members are more involved in club decisions than in many other countries. This was evidenced when the club signed a deal with arms manufacturer Rheinmetall two years ago and in the case of Nmecha as well. When the midfielder signed for Dortmund in 2023, many of the club's fans protested because the player had previously shared or liked several transphobic and homophobic posts on his Instagram account. In response, Nmecha deleted some posts and instead issued a statement emphasizing "I do not discriminate against anyone.".

Article 4 of German Basic Law guarantees that each individual is allowed to decide how strongly, why and which god to believe in. In football, players cannot display political, religious, or personal slogans, statements, or images on their jerseys, undershirts, or gear. However, physical gestures are allowed so long as they don't delay the game or antagonize the crowd.

The use of physical religious gestures has history in sports, as professor Paul Putz described in his book "The Spirit of the Game: American Christianity and Major-Time Sports". Putz describes how the the pioneers of the Christian athlete movement realized they: "could influence others to Christian ideals more effectively on the field than in the pulpit.".

Sources indicate that and yet, such gestures can also be at odds with the atmosphere of modern sports arenas, particularly football. In their book "Sports and Christianity: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives", Nick J. Watson and Andrew Parker explain how modern sport has become a substitute for traditional faith.

"Sport seduces the teeming 'global village'; it is the new opiate of the masses; it is one of the great modern experiences … Sport, for many, has replaced religion as a source of emotional catharsis and spiritual passion," they wrote.

With the 26-year-old Nmecha a key player for both club and country, the conversation around faith and football looks set to continue for some time yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there’s one thing Brighton and Hove Albion know how to do, it’s sell players for sizeable fees and replace them with bargain signings who prove to be just as good, if not better.

Sources indicate that they replaced Yves Bissouma with Moises Caicedo, Robert Sanchez with Bart Verbruggen, Leandro Trossard with Kaoru Mitoma, and Marc Cucurella with Pervis Estupinan. Even when Caicedo and Alexis Mac Allister departed in the same summer, Brighton managed to maintain their upward trajectory thanks in part to the emergence of Carlos Baleba.

Now, having sold Baleba to Manchester United for £70 million, the Seagulls appear to have pulled off the same trick with another promising young midfielder: Chema Andres, who has developed a formidable partnership with veteran Pascal Gross in midfield.

Sources indicate that andres was still developing in Real Madrid’s academy less than two years ago. After honing his skills in the Spanish capital, he joined Stuttgart in 2025 for €3 million, where he rapidly established himself as an important figure in midfield, steering them to a DFB-Pokal final and Champions League qualification.

Industry observers note that he appeared destined to continue his development in Germany, but Brighton had other ideas. With just hours left in the summer transfer window, the Seagulls swooped in and signed him for £16 million. Fabian Hurzeler thrust him in at the deep end, and Andres quickly repaid his trust by assisting on his debut at Coventry and leading Brighton to an EFL Cup victory at Old Trafford.

A midfield masterclass from @BHAFC's Chema Andres 👏 https://t.co/9s4FUF7Kd2October 3, 2026.

Sources indicate that in just his second season of senior football, Andres is emerging as one of the Premier League’s top midfielders. Brighton sit second in the table, five points behind Arsenal, one ahead of Manchester City and 14 clear of relegation-threatened Manchester United. At the heart of their start is Andres, whose defensive discipline and penetrative passing has made him indispensable after Baleba's departure.

Recent findings suggest that while Baleba’s greatest strength lies in his ball-carrying ability, Andres offers Brighton a different route through opposition defenses. According to Gradient Sports, a football analysis tech giant, Andres is averaging 4.41 midfield line-breaking passes per 90 minutes, compared with Baleba’s 2.74 during his final season at Brighton. He is also completing 79.2% of these passes, well above Baleba’s 70.9%.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

It has been revealed that that superiority extends to more audacious, high-risk passes: Andres is attempting 2.02 attacking line-breaking passes per 90, nearly twice Baleba’s 1.05, while completing them with far greater accuracy (90.9% vs. 71.4%). Whereas Baleba relied on his explosive acceleration to bypass opponents, Andres is using his vision, composure and passing range to slice through defensive lines and find his teammates.

According to recent reports, andres is also making his presence felt off the ball. While he might not be the same all-action midfielder who thrives on charging around the pitch and throwing himself into duels, his positional awareness and anticipation have proved invaluable in shielding Brighton’s backline. No Premier League midfielder has registered more tackles per 90 (3.31) or blocks per 90 (2.94) than Andres this season, while his 64.7% success rate in 50/50 duels exceeds Baleba’s 62.5%.

At 21 years-old, Andres is already imposing himself against the Premier League’s top sides. He excelled against Bruno Guimaraes and Declan Rice and found the back of the net in a 3–0 victory against defending champions Arsenal, before holding his own in a 1-0 win against Manchester City.

Despite costing Brighton less than a tenth of what City spent on Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez combined, Andrés helped the Seagulls secure their first away victory against City in 18 attempts, before playing a pivotal role in their hard-fought 2–0 win against Brentford.

For all his virtues, it would be premature to declare Andrés an outright upgrade on Baleba. Nevertheless, his passing intelligence, defensive anticipation and tactical discipline could make him an even better fit for Hurzeler’s system. Rather than simply replacing Baleba’s qualities, Brighton have found a midfielder whose strengths complement their style of play, once again demonstrating their knack for staying one step ahead of the transfer market.

For a club that has built its reputation on unearthing hidden gems, molding them into stars, and selling them for astronomical profits, Andres is shaping up to be another transfer masterstroke. And if he can help Brighton secure a maiden Champions League qualification, Baleba’s departure might be remembered not as a setback, but as the catalyst for the greatest moment in the club’s history.

Sources indicate that after getting his major breakthrough as the co-founder of the football analytics website Breaking The Lines, Zachary Lowy has been able to tap into his footballing expertise for a number of esteemed outlets like ESPN, FotMob, The Times, The Independent and Urban Pitch. Since joining FourFourTwo as a freelancer in 2025, Lowy has been able to cover a wide range of topics from analyzing the sweeping changes to the MLS season to interviewing key figures like Asamoah Gyan and Rob Holding. Fluent in Spanish, Portuguese and Italian, Lowy’s versatile skillset has allowed him to traverse a number of different fields when covering major competitions like the FIFA Club World Cup. In addition to football, he is also a seasoned participant of other sports like pickleball, tennis, and volleyball.

Industry News: Mauricio Pochettino's final go with USMNT is all about pivoting to the future before Manchester United move

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1168 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three days after tearing up as he revealed his departure from the U.S.
  • After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity.
  • Sources indicate that "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he remarked on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three days after tearing up as he revealed his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino stated he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

Sources indicate that "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he remarked on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that indicates it's not key tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

Pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his looks for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

Industry observers note that "What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the latest coaches that arrive here," Pochettino said. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

For all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

According to recent reports, for perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an crucial new chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

As for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his new role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

Recent findings suggest that two years removed from starting a upcoming job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-important clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

"For me, it's not difficult," he stated of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most important [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are currently in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

#83185. THE BREAKDOWN: The real reasons why Enzo Maresca's Man City can't stop losing - from anonymous Enzo Fernandez abandoning Elliot Anderson, to the fatal flaws in Italian's set-up that are being brutally exposed

THE BREAKDOWN: The real reasons why Enzo Maresca's Man City can't stop losing - from anonymous Enzo Fernandez abandoning Elliot Anderson, to the fatal flaws in Italian's set-up that are being brutally exposed

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1744 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 14:40 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.
  • Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a new manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 14:40 EST, 20 November 2026.

Diet Pep is losing his fizz. Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.

Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a new manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.

Three months in, and three defeats on the spin that left them six points behind Arsenal have made it clear that something is not clicking for Maresca.

In a recent development, is the uncertainty around the potential punishment following that guilty verdict taking its toll? Is Maresca just suffering from his usual late autumn dips? He suffered similar tricky periods around late October and early November at Leicester and his first season at Chelsea too.

Or is there something at the heart of his side, of his system, that’s finally being exposed?

Enzo Maresca's Man City have slumped to three straight Premier League defeats after a promising start to the season.

Recent findings suggest that guardiola’s City was all about control. Keep the ball, dominate the pitch, play the game at your pace, on your terms.

Maresca’s City, regardless of how well they started the season, has been about anything but. It has been about triumph amid chaos, about moments of magic more than the overarching method.

Industry observers note that without that control, City’s defensive concerns have been laid bare. The 13 goals they have let in after 10 games is their most at this stage since 2008. They haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last eight matches in all competitions. That's a drought longer than at any point under Guardiola.

Their biggest problem over City's three successive Premier League defeats is just how susceptible they have been to counter attacks.

Only Newcastle have faced more shots this season following ‘fast breaks’ – data giants Opta's term for counter attacks – than City’s 17, and 11 of those have come in the last three games: six against Nottingham Forest, two of which led to goals, three against Brighton and another two against Aston Villa.

Maresca’s side are being more profligate in possession, too. Over the first seven games of the season, they lost the ball 120 times a game on average – one of the best figures in the division. Since then, it’s closer to 140.

City have been wasteful in possession and regularly overrun on the counter, with Elliot Anderson (centre) too often left isolated in midfield.

ANDERSON CAN'T DO IT ALL ON HIS OWN.

Many of these problems have their roots in Maresca's serious problems in midfield. Rodri, the best holding midfielder of his generation, was always going to be hard to replace but Maresca appears to be expecting Elliot Anderson to do it all on his own.

According to recent reports, anderson is at his best when he’s free to get up and down the pitch, box to box, using his physicality not just in winning the ball back but progressing it. No midfielder played more passes into the final third last season than Anderson at Forest. At one stage of the campaign, he had played more progressive passes than any other player across Europe’s top five leagues.

And yet Maresca is forcing Anderson to play as the sitter while his golden boy Enzo Fernandez, whom he pushed City to sign in the summer for £125million, is roaming free and high up the pitch.

Maresca likes his teams to build up in a 3-1-6 shape, which sees Fernandez push up as an extra attacking midfielder, and leaves Anderson manning the fort alone.

When City lose the ball, though, it leaves them wide open.

This is the opening goal City conceded against Forest. Josko Gvardiol wants to play the ball inside but has only red shirts and empty green space ahead of him. Anderson is the only man free, but even he is too high and has a Forest player ready to cut off the pass. Eventually, Gvardiol gets robbed and Forest score.

A lack of options for Josko Gvardiol (left) led to Forest's opener against City. Enzo Fernandez (circled) was caught high up the pitch, way ahead of the deeper Anderson (also circled).

Here’s another moment in the defeat by Brighton.

According to recent reports, the Seagulls break forward on the flank and Anderson races over to close the ball down. Fernandez is, you guessed it, high up the pitch.

City have no midfield cover to stop the ball inside, Abdukodir Khusanov gets drawn in and leaves loads of space in behind for Yasin Ayari to exploit and cross to Maxim De Cuyper for a great chance.

The lack of protection offered by Anderson and especially the more advanced Fernandez was again on show against Brighton, who were able to exploit the acres of space left in midfield.

Recent findings suggest that fernandez is doing what Maresca wants, but it’s not working. Maresca needs more from him, especially when Anderson’s instincts are to press and harass and bully, which can leave gaps when he does not yet read the game as comprehensively as Rodri.

Industry observers note that anderson sits in the top five for ball recoveries among midfielders to have played 500 minutes this season. Fernandez is in the bottom five. That figure becomes even more alarming when you consider Anderson has created more chances from open play than Fernandez, too.

Industry observers note that ayyoub Bouaddi revealed at the World Cup that he had the most similar profile to Rodri. It might be time for Maresca to put some faith in him.

Sources indicate that maresca has always wanted his goalkeeper to be an 11th outfielder. In his one season at Leicester, Mads Hermansen played more passes than any goalkeeper in Championship history. During his time at Chelsea, there was a shaky moment in a draw with Arsenal when loud groans greeted a misplaced pass from Robert Sanchez.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I am the guy who asks Robert to do that,’ mentioned Maresca after that game. ‘The moment he stops doing that, he is not going to play.’.

According to recent reports, donnarumma, though, for all his (usually) excellent shot-stopping, is anything but a ball-playing goalkeeper. The ball rolled under his foot from a simple back pass against Coventry and so nearly crept over the line. He gifted France an early lead while on international duty with Italy when he passed the ball straight to Michael Olise.

Only two keepers made more errors leading to shots than Donnarumma across the course of last season, with many of those being with his feet, like when he gifted Kai Havertz an equaliser in City's victory over Arsenal in April.

Gianluigi Donnarumma has never been good with his feet - now his excellent shot-stopping has taken a dip too.

The Italian should have easily dealt with Nicolas Jackson's second goal in City's 2-1 loss at Aston Villa.

The decision to let James Trafford leave in the summer, especially with Guardiola’s impending departure and a manager like Maresca coming in, is looking ever more misguided.

Recent findings suggest that trafford is not immune to mistakes either, of course. He erred badly when trying to play out from the back for City against Spurs last season and made an almost identical howler for Leeds at Bournemouth in October. But he is still far more confident at playing out from the back than Donnarumma.

The double blow for Maresca is that the trade-off with Donnarumma – where he makes up for his weakness with the ball at his feet by making saves that other keepers can’t make – is no longer paying off either.

Nicolas Jackson’s shot squirmed straight through him to hand Villa victory and condemn City to their first defeat of the season.

When you are coughing up chances as frequently as City are, Maresca needs his keeper to be on top form.

It has been revealed that do you know who is keeping the ball out of his net? James Trafford. He boasts the highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in the top flight, keeping out 81 per cent of the shots on target coming his way. Donnarumma is 15th, on less than 66 per cent.

According to Opta’s expected data, Trafford has also prevented more than four goals that he should have conceded from the quality of the shots he’s faced. Again, he’s the best in the Premier League. Donnarumma is middle of the pack.

Sources indicate that ‘At the moment, I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation,’ said Maresca recently. Without Trafford there and just 34-year-old Geronimo Rulli as back-up, he doesn’t really have a choice but to persist with Donnarumma and hope he improves.

When the goals stop flowing for Erling Haaland, City can't mask all their other problems.

So used are we now to seeing the Norwegian on the scoresheet, having notched nine in City’s opening eight matches, that when he goes just two games without a goal it feels as if he’s on a barren spell.

The problem, though, is less down to Haaland and more that City’s build-up in recent weeks is struggling to get him into the game.

Recent findings suggest that city are finding it more difficult to get Haaland on the ball. His touches per game are falling steadily but, crucially, so are the quality of the chances his team-mates are creating for him.

Haaland had more than one Opta-defined 'big chance' in five of City’s opening seven games. He’s had just one come his way in each of their three defeats.

Recent findings suggest that his expected goals (xG) tally is dropping too. Across City’s winning streak, Haaland’s average xG per match was 0.81. Only once, against Liverpool, did it drop below 0.5.

Over the three defeats, it’s just 0.45 and has not once gone above 0.5.

Antoine Semenyo missing the last three games through injury has not helped, especially when teams now try to pack the middle of the pitch and force City wide.

Haaland will come good, he always does, but City need to start serving him again if Maresca wants to get through this tricky spell and stop the vultures from circling.

#83179. Latest Update: This boiled bag of offal is banned in the US. In Scotland it's a fine-dining treat

📅 03 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1498 w)

Latest Update: This boiled bag of offal is banned in the US. In Scotland it's a fine-dining treat

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1498 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • But even the late, great American chef, writer and television host recognized that Scotland’s national dish, with its “sinister sheep parts” wrapped in a shroud of mystery and half-invented history, could be a hard sell.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Don’t let them tell you otherwise, that’s really one of life’s great pleasures,” Bourdain said on one of his gastro-curious pilgrimages to Glasgow.
  • A mash-up of diced lung, liver and heart mixed with oatmeal, beef suet, onion and assorted spices, haggis was traditionally made by stuffing these raw ingredients into the stomach of a recently slain sheep and boiling the lot to a state of palatability.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthony Bourdain loved haggis. But even the late, great American chef, writer and television host recognized that Scotland’s national dish, with its “sinister sheep parts” wrapped in a shroud of mystery and half-invented history, could be a hard sell.

Recent findings suggest that “Don’t let them tell you otherwise, that’s really one of life’s great pleasures,” Bourdain said on one of his gastro-curious pilgrimages to Glasgow. “There is no more unfairly reviled food on Earth than the haggis.”.

A mash-up of diced lung, liver and heart mixed with oatmeal, beef suet, onion and assorted spices, haggis was traditionally made by stuffing these raw ingredients into the stomach of a recently slain sheep and boiling the lot to a state of palatability.

In a recent development, instagrammable is not the word that immediately comes to mind. In our 21st-century world, where “clean” eating and processed pap overlap, haggis can seem like an “Outlander”-style outlier from another age.

Yet, by some alchemy, once cooked to its required “warm-reekin’ (steaming)” state, it adds up to much more than the sum of its modest parts. It’s offaly charm has kept nose-to-tail eating alive among a younger generation of Scots that has largely turned its back on the tripe, liver and kidneys their predecessors enjoyed (or endured).

Carefully prepared, haggis tastes both oaty and meaty; it is dark and crumbly, a little crispy at the edges but still moist; earthy but also savory and spicy; deep-tasting and profoundly warming, the perfect foil for its traditional garnish of floury mashed potatoes and orange bashed turnip.

“It’s like a cuddle for the stomach,” indicates Nicola Turner, a 35-year-old office administrator from Helensburgh, a town on western Scotland’s Firth of Clyde.

For children of the 1960s and ’70s, like crime novelist Ian Rankin, haggis meals were a choice between the classic meat-and-two-veg plate and the battered and deep-fried, chip-shop iteration loved by both his friend Bourdain and his quintessentially Scottish detective character, Inspector John Rebus.

Now myriad other treatments have blossomed.

“I’m pretty sure the first time I dined with AB in Edinburgh we had haggis in filo pastry with a jam-style – maybe blackcurrant – sauce,” Rankin recalled. “He was a major fan of haggis and of chip shops. Rebus will have enjoyed the occasional haggis supper from his local chip shop. He was definitely a fan, as am I.”.

“It is all about the spicing and the texture,” notes the Scottish food writer, novelist and cook Sue Lawrence, a champion of haggis’ adaptability for use in other dishes. “If you didn’t know what was in it, you wouldn’t think ‘oh that tastes of liver or whatever.’ It is all nicely chopped up and the oatmeal gives it a lovely texture. It could easily be a nice, massive mince dish.”.

These US restaurants and chefs are James Beard Award finalists.

Lawrence uses haggis as an alternative to beef and pork ragù in lasagna and in her pastilla, a version of the North African dish in which a hand-made haggis from the Isle of Mull substitutes for the traditional poultry or seafood filling. The filo pastry savory is flavored with the spice blend ras el hanout, apricots, chile, orange zest and almonds before being sprinkled with cinnamon and icing sugar.

Such cultural crossovers serve as a reminder that haggis could easily be a dish with nothing specifically Scottish about it at all. Records of similar quick and portable preparations of the fast-perishing innards of sheep and other animals date back to ancient Rome and Greece.

Haggis-like combinations of offal and grains are part of the culinary history of several countries. Spain has chireta, Romania drob and Sweden polsa, while chaudin, or ponce, is a rice and meat-stuffed pig stomach that is a staple of Cajun cooking.

In neighboring England, recipes for “hagese,” “hagws of a schepe,” “haggas” or “haggus” pop up in recipe books published between the 15th and 17th centuries, probably preceding written records north of the border.

Etymological evidence points to the term “haggis” having its roots in Old Norse, suggesting an early version of an oat-and-offal sausage might have arrived in Britain and Ireland on a Viking longboat.

But ever since it was first optioned by the poet Robert Burns in the late 1700s, the haggis backstory has been monopolized by Scotland and the Scots, sometimes mischievously.

It is, according to the kind of lore that Burns engendered, the dish a doughty Highlander would carry with him as he drove cattle through the glens to the markets of the central belt or the perfect picnic for a whisky smuggler plying his illicit trade by moonlight.

From such romantic notions it was a short step to turning the haggis into a wee wild beastie, one with longer legs on one side that was thus condemned to run round and round whichever hill it lived on. In 2003, a poll of American tourists in Scotland found that one in three of them believed they might encounter such a confused creature on a Caledonian vacation.

Bourdain, a native New Yorker, may have qualified as haggis’ biggest admirer since Burns, but his compatriots at the US Department of Agriculture remain unconverted to offal-filled paunch. Haggis imports into the United States were prohibited in 1971 as part of a ban on the consumption of all livestock lungs. Authentic versions of old school haggis remain culinary contraband in the US, as hard to lay your hands on as Cuban cigars.

Across the rest of the world, it’s a different story. According to leading producer Simon Howie, haggis is more widely appreciated and consumed now than it has been since Burns improvised his “Address to a Haggis” for the entertainment of well-to-do Edinburgh acquaintances.

Firmly tongue-in-cheek, the poem lauds the “Great chieftain o’ the pudding race,” as exactly the kind of unpretentious, hearty fare required to nourish a nation of braveheart warriors.

In comparison to the enfeebling foreign muck enjoyed by the capital’s claret-quaffing elites of the time – the olio, fricassée or ragoût that would “sicken a sow” – Burns urges his readers to wonder at the magical impact of haggis on his fellow sons of Scotland’s soil.

As the English translation of the original Scots language version puts it:.

But mark the Rustic, haggis-fed/.

The trembling earth resounds his tread/.

Clap in his ample fist a blade/.

And legs and arms and heads will cut/.

These days synthetic casings have largely replaced stomach but ovine and porcine innards remain at the core of most of the haggis produced in its homeland, stated Howie, who estimates that his firm Simon Howie Butchers, accounts for around 60% of the roughly two million haggises produced every year.

According to recent reports, for Howie, versatility, value for money and convenience explain why this staple of the Scottish larder is thriving. Typically haggis retails in Scotland, which accounts for half of global consumption by volume, for around £6, or $7.70 per kilogram ($3.36/pound). That’s around half the price of less expensive cuts of beef or a third of the price of Scotch lamb while enjoying a fairly similar nutritional and calorific profile.

Best Mexican food: 23 dishes to try.

“You can give your kids a meal that is not full of things you don’t want to feed them – for a few pounds you can feed three strapping lads,” Howie said.

According to recent reports, “From a kitchen perspective, it is very simple because when it leaves our factory it is already cooked. So when you or a restaurant owner gets it into the kitchen all you have to do is heat it up to be piping hot. It couldn’t be more basic: a student with no cooking skills or a Michelin-starred chef do exactly the same thing to put it out on the plate.”.

Its texture means haggis can also be usefully deployed in fine dining alongside leaner meat like venison or as a stuffing for poultry and game birds. Its spicy intensity means it is also finding uses in canapés and as a crouton-borne garnish for soups.

Buoyant sales are also underpinned by the increasing consumption of haggis in forms inspired by Scotland’s ethnic minorities.

Glasgow’s Sikh community pioneered haggis pakora in the 1990s and samosas, spring rolls and quesadillas have followed in its wake, often using a vegetarian version of the protein in which the offal is replaced by a mix of vegetables, pulses and mushrooms.

It has been revealed that such dishes are more than culinary twists. They are badges of belonging, and an indication that, two centuries after Burns grabbed it for the nation, haggis is as intimately entwined with Scots identity as ever.

Just ask Ross O’Cinneide, a promising 14-year-old fly-half in the junior section of Stirling County rugby club.

“Most of my friends and I like haggis,” he notes. “Mum makes it for us sometimes after rugby and it’s got a very nice warming feeling. And it’s nice because it’s purely Scottish.”.

Anthropic IPO: four ways the AI giant wants to disrupt science

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1239 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.
  • Recent findings suggest that anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence company, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
  • It has been revealed that the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence company, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. With a staggering valuation of around US$1.5 trillion, the firm, based in San Francisco, California, is now among the world’s most valuable companies — and it has major ambitions in science.

It has been revealed that the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI. Its models have proven powerful in research, and Anthropic has launched its own directed science effort, focusing on areas including quantum mechanics and protein design. This year alone, it has reported mathematics breakthroughs and launched its first life sciences laboratory.

The IPO might also unleash a historic wave of philanthropy: all seven of Anthropic’s founders are likely to become billionaires and have pledged to donate 80% of their equity in the company to charity, including chief executive Dario Amodei. And on 18 October, the company revealed that it had established the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, created to support initiatives that benefit society and stocked with an initial commitment of 5% of Anthropic’s shares.

But the firm has drawn criticism from researchers, who say its aims of curing diseases on short timescales are unrealistic and that its race towards developing ultra-powerful, ‘superintelligent’ AI models pose serious risks, including an existential threat to humanity. In its public prospectus, published ahead of the IPO, Anthropic outlines a latest governance structure that it claims is “consistent with our commitment to AI safety and responsibility”, and adds that safety research directly shapes the firm’s “model design, training, and deployment.”.

Nature looks at four areas of science where Anthropic is making waves.

Recent findings suggest that AI’s potential to turbocharge the discovery of new medicines has been a centerpiece of Anthropic’s pitch to investors. “If today we look at things like cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness — these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” Amodei remarked in a promotional video ahead of the IPO.

The manufacturer has been rapidly expanding its biomedical ambitions. This year, Anthropic opened its first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research, announced partnerships with several pharmaceutical companies, and noted it was pursuing drug leads of its own. “We initiative to scale this work up substantially from here,” the company said on 27 October.

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

But Amodei’s habit of promising swift, AI-fueled cures for complex diseases has rankled many researchers and entrepreneurs in the field who feel the timeline is unrealistic.

Industry observers note that over the last year, Anthropic has made a major push in the life sciences. In June, the company hired John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel Prize for his work on AlphaFold2 while at Google DeepMind in London.

Recent findings suggest that some of the company’s early biological research received a mixed reception from biologists. After Anthropic reported using a swarm of AI agents to find signs of a upcoming CRISPR-like system in viral sequence data, some researchers questioned the novelty of the finding and noted that the company had not carried out the experimental work needed to determine the system’s function.

In a recent development, in protein design — a field that has boomed thanks to specialist AI tools including AlphaFold — Anthropic’s work has also failed to generate much excitement. In August, Anthropic used Claude Science — an agentic system that can access other biological tools and databases — to make novel ‘binders’ against 15 protein targets.

Recent findings suggest that “Expectations are sky high,” notes Anthony Gitter, a computational biologist at the Morgridge Institute for Research in Madison, Wisconsin. “I understand why some view their initial public results as underwhelming.”.

But Gitter is enthusiastic about Anthropic’s protein design efforts, largely because the firm was transparent about the work, from the prompts it used to the sequences that were generated. “I would strongly encourage Anthropic to continue that in their future life sciences research,” Gitter adds.

In recent months, Anthropic and other companies — notably Google DeepMind and OpenAI — have been working to establish their research credentials in large part by showing off the rapidly growing mathematical abilities of their flagship AI models.

On 7 September Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge and collaborator Tristan Buckmaster at Fresh York University solved a special case of the Navier-Stokes equations, a long-standing problem in mathematical physics that describes the flow of fluids. Hours after Anthropic confirmed the result, OpenAI claimed a full solution of the problem, igniting a controversy.

Recent findings suggest that in another collaboration, Alpöge and mathematical physicist Ethan Sussman at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, have been working towards establishing the mathematical foundations of the standard model of particle physics. This too is a problem on which OpenAI has made similar claims.

Anthropic and its competitors see the ability to write a rigorous proof of a mathematical fact as a crucial testing ground for their reasoning models. That’s in large part because the correctness of a proof is an objective measure that can be used as a ‘reward’ to further train AI systems.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • During Mauricio Pochettino's tenure, Matt Freese has been his starting keeper, taking over during the Gold Cup and starting every game that he was available for until the September/October international window, when Pochettino used Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake.
  • Following that match, Kochen acknowledged that the USMNT squad has done a lot to put him in this position, and he'll know that even if Pochettino won't be the manager choosing the lineups, performances like this one will be crucial for how the USMNT keeper picture looks moving forward.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, historically, goalkeeper has been a position of strength for the United States men's national team, to the extent that during the time of Tim Howard and Brad Guzan, both were playing Premier League soccer, but only one could start between the sticks. Things have changed since then, with numerous keepers coming through the ranks over the years, with most playing domestically or sitting on the bench for stronger European sides. However, that could be coming to an end for the team.

During Mauricio Pochettino's tenure, Matt Freese has been his starting keeper, taking over during the Gold Cup and starting every game that he was available for until the September/October international window, when Pochettino used Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake. Kochen, who is playing his first season of first-team soccer at Lyngby in Denmark (where center back Neil Pierre also got his first taste of senior soccer), got the clean sheet against Mexico during that camp and turned that into a start against Haiti in Concacaf Nations League play in his native Miami, setting the USMNT up well to advance to the semifinals of the tournament.

Following that match, Kochen acknowledged that the USMNT squad has done a lot to put him in this position, and he'll know that even if Pochettino won't be the manager choosing the lineups, performances like this one will be crucial for how the USMNT keeper picture looks moving forward.

Industry observers note that "I feel like I've grown quite a lot," Kochen said following the match, reflecting on his adjustment to the national team. "I'm getting used to competing at the international level, but I've just got to give it to my team because they've been unbelievable. They make it so easy to just come out here and play free and be me, so without them, this wouldn't be possible.".

According to recent reports, his growth is evident; one of the first things that comes to mind when watching the 20-year-old is his poise. Kochen had the ball at his feet plenty, completing all 20 of his passes to help send the attack on its way, and also made the two saves that he needed to on a mostly quiet night. His age also revealed when Haiti scored with him out of position, a goal that was called back for offside, but you take the good with the bad for young players because that's a learning moment, and as he earns more reps at the senior level, those are the kind of mistakes that can be ironed out.

Industry observers note that "I'm not saying he hasn't played games in Barcelona, but at the senior level, every game he plays, he gets better and better and better," one of Kochen's coaches, Andreas Bjelland, told CBS Sports. "Because understanding the full-pitch play, and not only being on the line, just taking shots, and being a training goalie, but now he's playing for points every week. He's growing as a player, as a person, and as somebody we can trust more and more in the stuff we do. So it's nice to see that it has come to this ... It's quite impressive.".

Recent findings suggest that you can't teach poise, and spending more than five years in the Barcelona system shows in how Kochen carries himself. It's becoming more common in American soccer for young players to test themselves abroad or to get into Major League Soccer teams at a younger age, and when they succeed, it goes a long way developmentally, as Kochen's case shows.

Industry observers note that "He is a person who trusts himself a lot. That's also why he's a good goalie, that at such a young age he hasn't that substantial of a doubt of himself," Mikkel Jespersen, Lyngby's other coach mentioned. "He knows what he's capable of doing, and that's really important as a goalie: that you trust yourself and know what things you are doing is something that can succeed in a longer period.".

While it's unknown what the next USMNT manager will value in a keeper, being able to perform in an uncertain environment with your coach having one foot out the door is something that will go a long way for Kochen's chances. In keeper terms, Kochen has plenty of time ahead of him, as players at his position regularly play until their late 30s or early 40s, so if he can continue this trajectory, the question of who protects the net could be solved for the foreseeable future.

Of course, that's a lot of projecting, but when the next generation of the USMNT is developing at an astounding rate, it's only natural to think about where players like Kochen could end up. Doing this in only his first season of professional soccer is already impressive, but the best is yet to come.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

According to recent reports, roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur.

Did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

According to recent reports, even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

“I am really aware of the situation,” Sage said. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”.

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

The challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

Recent findings suggest that it was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be stated of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

It was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

According to recent reports, “Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi noted. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We showed our maturity. We are improving.”.

“I was very nervous before the game, during the game, after the red card, it’s always better playing with one player more. But today, against this team, they played with this behaviour, all behind the line of the ball, aggressive. Very tough game.”.

In a recent development, when asked if Spurs are looking up the table, he replied: “We don’t forget the ambitions. We have to look behind what was the situation two weeks ago. Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

In a recent development, last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”.

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with teams coming shortly.
